items.title: Iran: Strait of Hormuz Will Not Reopen Until Conditions Are Met
Iran says Hormuz Strait to remain closed until US meets seven conditions
items.summary: Iran says Hormuz Strait to remain closed until US meets seven conditions Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has said that the Strait of Hormuz will remain shut until Washington meets certain conditions. Ghalibaf, who also acts as Tehran's chief negotiator in the talks, said that the contested waterway will remain closed until seven conditions based on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding are met by Washington. He conceded that the US had made "some proposals through a mediator" after Tehran presented a seven-day roadmap to reopen the strait. But he warned Washington that "the era of wasting time and dictating unilateral demands is over" and Iran's position remains "clear and definite".

A spokesperson for Yemen's armed forces, which are aligned with the internationally recognised government, said forces were targeting what he described as "vital targets", without providing further details. Yemen's Houthi-run Al Masirah TV reported earlier an attack it said was carried out by Saudi Arabia on Sanaa. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation on the report. The conflict between the Iran-backed Houthis and forces aligned with the Saudi-backed government mostly stopped after a 2022 truce, but fighting has broken out again in a spillover from the wider war between Iran and the United States. Hostilities resumed this year after the Houthis declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in July and began attacking Saudi territory and shipping, while Houthi forces also made major territorial gains along Yemen's Red Sea coast. items.title: Trump rejects Iranian proposal to open Hormuz and end war
items.summary: Trump rejects Iranian proposal to open Hormuz and end war US President Donald Trump said on Saturday he had rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the Iran war. Iran raised the initiative at the UN General Assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted to the Americans via Qatari mediators and that it could reopen the strategic waterway and put an end to hostilities in the region within seven days. But in comments to reporters at the White House, Trump said: "I reject their proposal. ... I rejected their deal. "They want to make a deal to open the Hormuz Strait immediately because they're losing so badly," he said before leaving for Tennessee. "We're winning tremendously. "They want to make a deal and I think that's fine, I like making a deal too. What they want to do is immediately open the Hormuz Strait ... because they have no money coming in, because they get their money from the Hormuz Strait," Trump said.

items.summary: Iran’s seven-day timetable would restart nuclear talks, but will the US be willing to deliver on terms that include reining in Israel in Lebanon? Iran’s seven-day timetable to reopen the strait of Hormuz and start talks on its nuclear programme has been pitched as a deal that could rapidly extricate Donald Trump from a political crisis but requires the US president to make difficult concessions. In the five days left before the proposed reopening of the strait, which is expected to relieve pressure on global energy markets, Trump would need to lift Iranian asset freezes, permit Iran to export its oil and, probably most difficult of all, order Benjamin Netanyahu to end Israel’s attacks on Hezbollah in Lebanon, thus achieving the “ceasefire on all fronts”. Iranian airlines mainly carry Iraqi Shia pilgrims to Iran's holy cities or Iranians visiting sacred sites in Iraq. The flights also serve Iraqi students studying in Iran and patients seeking medical treatment there. It said Baghdad had secured "an agreement allowing Iranian airlines, with the exception of Mahan Air, to operate 40 flights daily to and from Najaf" , a city sacred to Shia Muslims. items.title: Trump says US may request Europe to release diesel from emergency stockpiles
items.summary: Trump says US may request Europe to release diesel from emergency stockpiles US President Donald Trump indicated that Washington could request European countries to release diesel from their emergency stockpiles, amid the war on Iran's impact on global fuel supplies. "We may ask them to do that," Trump told reporters on Thursday. Meanwhile, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said European states should do so "immediately". "Our European partners should accelerate delivery on their existing commitments and make additional supplies immediately available to address ongoing disruptions," he wrote in a post on X. "American farmers, truckers, and businesses should not be left carrying the burden of a global diesel shortage. America is doing its part. We look to our allies to match their commitments with action."

Speaking at a news conference, Baghaei said that Tehran is "focusing on the strait foremost", and that its primary concern is "to reach a solution and to have peace and stability restored within this waterway".  He added that, by contrast, Washington's strategy to end the conflict is focused on Iran's nuclear file. He told reporters that the return of International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) inspectors has not been discussed by Iran's leadership. He noted that the peace process has been thwarted by the "volatility and fluctuation" of Washington's decision-making. “This is reflected in their conflicting statements as well as their fluctuating demands. State Department says Iranian UN delegation duo expelled from US
items.summary: State Department says Iranian UN delegation duo expelled from US The United States has expelled two members of the Iranian delegation who attended the recent UN General Assembly after they ignored an order to leave the country, the State Department said Saturday. "Two more members of the Iranian delegation were found still in (New York) long after the United Nations General Assembly had passed. They have now been kicked out of the US," a US official told AFP, adding that Secretary of State Marco Rubio "means business." US media reported the State Department had told Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his delegation to leave the country Monday, and resorted to expelling the two members after learning from the Iranian mission to the UN they remained in the country on Friday. One member of the delegation left Friday night, while the second departed Saturday morning, according to Axios.

items.summary: US arrests Energy Department employee under claims of backing Yemen’s Houthis The Justice Department has arrested a man under claims that he attempted to provide material support or resources to Yemen’s Houthis. The 51 year-old, identified as Ashton Hamed Ellaboudy, is a US Energy Department employee. "As alleged, a US government employee travelled overseas and used his specialised expertise in an attempt to aid the Houthis, a designated Foreign Terrorist Organization backed by Iran," the assistant attorney general for national security, John A Eisenberg, said. Eisenberg claimed that Ellaboudy "acquired materials for the construction of explosive material and drones capable of delivering these explosives". "These allegations are so deeply disturbing that they almost defy imagination," he added. Ellaboudy is scheduled to appear before a federal judge on 2 October in Washington.

items.summary: Trump 'surprised' UK freed air base suspects on bail US President Donald Trump said on Monday that British police should not have released on bail five men who were arrested near an air base used by the United States over a suspected attack. Trump added that the case "might be" linked to Iran but declined to give details. "I'm surprised that they released them; I wouldn't have done that," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office, while adding that British authorities had worked "very closely" with the US. "We know everything about them. We would not have released them." The five men were arrested early on Sunday near the Royal Air Force (RAF) Fairford base in southwest England, from which US bombers have taken off to target Iran since March.

items.title: Riyadh schools to operate remotely for week, AFP reports
items.summary: Riyadh schools to operate remotely for week, AFP reports Parents across Riyadh received emails from schools on Sunday announcing a last-minute plan to shift to remote learning for a week, according to messages seen by AFP. "We have just been informed by Saudi authorities that schools must remain closed all week," read two separate messages seen by AFP. There was no official reason given but the move comes amid heightened tensions in the Gulf and near-daily attacks aimed at Saudi Arabia by Iran-backed Houthi fighters in Yemen. "When a decision affects an entire school community for a full week, families deserve clear communication and transparency about the reasons behind it," one parent living in Riyadh who spoke on condition of anonymity told AFP. "It's a last-minute decision. We have no clue what's happening," a Lebanese expatriate living in Riyadh added. The announcement comes a day after the Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen's Houthis said it had intercepted drones and ballistic missiles targeting the kingdom. items.title: Iranian rial at new low, as cenbank sells dollars to support currency
items.summary: Iranian rial at new low, as cenbank sells dollars to support currency Iran's rial continued its decline on Saturday, as the central bank announced an injection of up to $2 billion to support the currency while the economy faces US sanctions and a naval blockade. The US dollar was sold at around 2.688 million rials, up from 2.632 million on Friday, according to free-market tracking website bon-bast.com, while alanchand.com reported 2.695 million rials per dollar. State television said state banks began selling up to $2 billion to support the currency, which has lost more than half of its value in the past year. With an inflation rate of more than 70 percent, life is becoming ever tougher for ordinary citizens unable to afford basic necessities or rent ​as a US blockade cuts the state's financial lifeline – oil exports. Many Iranians seeking safe havens for their savings have been buying dollars, other hard currencies or gold.

items.title: Lessons from the Iran War
items.summary: The Iran war offers broader lessons about the limits of force, the resilience of revolutionary regimes, and the unpredictability of modern conflict. Military action can weaken an adversary without producing decisive political outcomes, while economic pressure, alliances, energy markets, and public opinion can prove equally consequential. The conflict also exposed vulnerabilities in alliance coordination, munitions stocks, counter-drone capabilities, and strategic communication. Effective deterrence ultimately requires hard power, resilient partnerships, clear objectives, and the political will to sustain them.

items.summary: Colombia's new US-backed government cuts ties with Iran Colombia said on Thursday it had cut diplomatic ties with Iran, the latest Washington ally in Latin America to sever links with the US arch-foe. Colombia's new right-wing president, Abelardo de la Espriella, has redrawn Colombia's alliances since taking over from his leftist predecessor Gustavo Petro on 7 August with the full-throated endorsement of US President Donald Trump. De la Espriella's government accused the Iranian government of having ties to "narco-terrorist groups that threaten the security of the country," without giving proof of the allegations. Iran's foreign ministry hit back on Friday, calling the allegations "baseless claims". "It is clear that none of the claims put forward by the Colombian government to justify this decision are valid or logical, and that this decision has been made solely under the influence of the Zionist regime and the United States."

items.title: Colombia formally cuts ties with Iran
items.summary: Colombia formally cuts ties with Iran Colombia on Thursday announced that it formally severed diplomatic relations with Iran, citing it "deteriorated" in Tehran. The Foreign Ministry said the decision took effect on Saturday due to "national and hemispheric security concerns," accusing Iran of human rights violations as well as alleged links to international terrorist and narcoterrorist groups. "Colombia also took into account confirmed human rights violations, verified attacks against countries not involved in the Middle East conflict, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and the authorities' obstruction of the International Atomic Energy Agency's (IAEA) efforts to verify the scope of Iran's nuclear program," the ministry said. "These facts deteriorated Colombia’s trust in the government of the Islamic Republic of Iran."

Similar to NATO's Article 5, the pact stipulates that an attack on one ally constitutes an attack on all. "For international agreements to come into effect, parliamentary approval is needed. Iran's Intelligence Ministry, which made the arrests in southern Kerman province, said the suspects in Sirjan county were organised into networks to “lure teenagers and young people” and had prepared “large quantities of Molotov cocktails” to “damage urban surveillance cameras in preparation for street unrest and acts of sabotage”. The ministry also accused the groups of “violence and destruction” during the January nationwide protests.

clusters.headline: Three commercial vessels struck in Hormuz since 1 Oct, UKMTO says

items.title: Three commercial vessels struck in Hormuz since 1 Oct, UKMTO says
items.summary: Three commercial vessels struck in Hormuz since 1 Oct, UKMTO says Attacks on commercial ships witnessed a surge during the past three days, as at least three tankers were struck by unidentified projectiles in and around the Strait of Hormuz, according to United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) warnings. Early Saturday, UKMTO reported that a crude oil tanker was hit on its port side approximately 4 nautical miles east of Oman. A day earlier, an outbound vessel suffered a small fire and blackout, while a second crude tanker was struck nearby. On Thursday, a supertanker carrying 2.5 million barrels caught fire after being hit off Oman while transiting an unauthorised route, according to Iran's Fars news agency. In its weekly Voluntary Reporting Area Overview released on 2 October, UKMTO said 91 incidents of damage to vessels have been reported since February this year. Three tankers have been struck in and around the Strait of Hormuz since 1 October 2026. (AFP)

clusters.headline: Iran's warns 'half-a-century-old' UAE over claim on three Gulf islands

items.title: Iran's warns 'half-a-century-old' UAE over claim on three Gulf islands
items.summary: Iran's warns 'half-a-century-old' UAE over claim on three Gulf islands Ali Akbar Velayati, a senior adviser to Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, has warned the United Arab Emirates (UAE) against challenging Tehran and its sovereignty over three islands in the Persian Gulf. In a post on his X account, Velayati dismissed recent claims made by the UAE at the United Nations General Assembly regarding sovereignty over Greater Tunb, Lesser Tunb, and Abu Musa, saying the three islands will remain Iranian forever, according to IRNA. "A country whose political life does not reach half a century makes claims from the UN podium about islands that have been recorded under Iran's name in historical documents and maps of past centuries," Velayati said in the Farsi-language post. He added that the UAE should not "rely on foreign powers" for its security and should instead pursue good relations with its neighbours, IRNA reported. "The neighbour stays, and the guest goes… Regional experience has shown that imported security has an expiration date," said the former Iranian foreign minister.

items.title: Iran welcomes exit of US forces from Iraq, calls for Washington to be held accountable
items.summary: Iran welcomes exit of US forces from Iraq, calls for Washington to be held accountable Iran’s foreign ministry on Saturday has congratulated the Iraqi government and people on the exit of US and other foreign forces from Iraq. In a statement posted on its Telegram channel, the ministry said the withdrawal is “a very important and necessary step” towards consolidating Iraq’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and independence. It accused the US of causing “irreparable consequences” for Iraq and the region since the 2003 invasion, which it said was launched under the false pretext of “weapons of mass destruction”, and called for the US government to be held accountable for crimes committed during the occupation.

Ze zouden in contact hebben gestaan met iemand in het buitenland, mogelijk iemand uit Iran. clusters.headline: L'Inde et sa stratégie de corridors

items.title: L'Inde et sa stratégie de corridors
items.summary: En Inde, dès que l'on parle de sanctions contre la Russie ou bien l'Iran, c'est le transport qui en paye le prix. Fin septembre, le président américain Donald Trump a renforcé sa loi sur les tarifs douaniers contre la Russie. Ces sanctions s'adressent aussi à tous les pays qui commercent avec Moscou. Or, l'Inde, pénalisée par la guerre au Moyen-Orient et la fermeture du détroit d'Ormuz, a continué d'importer du pétrole russe. Dans ses derniers articles pour l'Institut de relations internationales et stratégiques (Iris), Olivier Da Lage, ancien journaliste à RFI et spécialiste de l'Inde, explique comment le pays cherche à bâtir de nouvelles routes pour diversifier son commerce.

Hij hoopt dat dat de binnenlandse brandstofprijzen doet dalen, in aanloop naar de tussentijdse verkiezingen begin november. clusters.headline: Red scare: Solid GOP districts reeling from war, price backlash

items.title: Red scare: Solid GOP districts reeling from war, price backlash
items.summary: On Monday, as the war with Iran crossed the seven-month mark, Governor Greg Abbott declared a statewide disaster in Texas as a result of a massive increase in diesel prices and a deepening fuel shortage. Texas is hardly alone. Diesel prices have climbed nationwide since the war began, with the national average now around $6.45 per gallon , up from $3.76 when the war began in late February, according to data from AAA. A number of other states have recently taken steps to try to ease the costs of gas and diesel amid the ongoing war. As the midterm elections near and the war’s costs hit voters’ wallets, Abbott's declaration is a window into a larger problem for Republicans across the country, including some in deep red states. Seen up close, it is a study in stasis and decline UN general assembly meetings are not usually riveting occasions. But this year’s encapsulated a world in flux and crisis, an international law and organisation structure that is falling apart, and a humanitarian order machine running hot. What unfolded was less a gathering for resolution and resolve than a display of showboating, frustration and fractiousness. It was a snapshot for the history books of four huge destabilising conflicts for which there seems to be no means of, or interest in, resolution – Ukraine, Iran, Palestine and Sudan. items.summary: Ethiopia is on the brink of another civil war. Last week, fighting between rebels and federal forces in the northern Tigray, Amhara, and Afar states left hundreds dead. These clashes may signal the start of a potentially devastating conflict in a country still recovering from a bloody civil war that killed approximately 600,000 people between 2020 and 2022. Fighting began as seven rebel groups from across various parts of the country announced the formation of a military coalition called the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival . The alliance’s expressed aim is to remove the federal government headed by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali from power. Major fighting has thus far remained confined to the northern Tigray state, where the previous civil war took place. clusters.headline: Hegseth says American forces have ‘destroyed’ Iran’s military

items.title: Hegseth says American forces have ‘destroyed’ Iran’s military
items.summary: Hegseth says American forces have ‘destroyed’ Iran’s military Secretary of War Pete Hegseth told a gathering of military leaders at Quantico Marine base on Wednesday that US forces have “destroyed” Iran’s navy, air force, defence systems, leadership and military-industrial capacity. Hegseth praised the American troops he addressed, crediting them with having destroyed Iran’s “entire defense space”. “Iran’s conventional shield has been crippled, and their nuclear ambitions have been crippled and laid bare for the world,” he added. Hegseth said the Pentagon has undergone a “clear break” from its past, with a “singular mission” of war-fighting. He said the department had fired “nearly 10 percent of the generals and admirals across the force”, a figure he framed as “accountability” rather than a “purge”, as some media have called it. Only the US was “capable of taking out the nuclear capability of Iran”, Rutte said, describing the country's nuclear programme as a potential near-term threat “not only for Israel and the Middle East” but for Europe as well. items.summary: The Iraq War was already four-years-old when I walked down the ramp of a C-17 at Al Taqaddum Air Base in April 2007. The fact that I am writing these words is proof that I survived that deployment and a subsequent one to Afghanistan in 2013. In the years since, I transitioned back into civilian life, established a new career, and saw my kids grow up and escape the nest. During nearly all of that time, there were still American troops on the ground in Iraq. I have a son serving in the military today. He has never been to Iraq, but I can absolutely sympathize with the Iraq veterans who came home from the war only to see their sons or daughters deploy to the same war zone. items.title: Venezuela blowback may have a long fuse. It always does.
items.summary: In 1927, Augusto Cesar Sandino began an insurgent campaign against the U.S. occupation of Nicaragua. Under orders from President Calvin Coolidge, the U.S. Marines had intervened in Nicaragua to settle a civil war between a conservative government and liberal rebels. In his manifesto , Sandino responded by effectively declaring war on the United States. He also specifically denounced former liberal leaders who had agreed to put down their arms in the face of U.S. intervention. Speaking of General Moncada, the leading liberal officer who had agreed to end his revolt in talks convened by future Secretary of State Henry Stimson, Sandino wrote: “Nobody gave him the authority to abandon the ranks of the revolution to make secret agreements with the enemy.” One imagines there are Chavistas in Venezuela with similar feelings about interim President Delcy Rodriguez right now. Having intervened to end the civil war in Nicaragua, the U.S. soon found itself embroiled in a bitter counter-insurgency campaign against Sandino’s men. clusters.headline: Vance describes Iran’s leadership as ‘very confused’, says deal possible

items.title: Vance describes Iran’s leadership as ‘very confused’, says deal possible
items.summary: Vance describes Iran’s leadership as ‘very confused’, says deal possible US Vice President JD Vance said there is still scope for a deal with Iran if its leaders honour their commitments to Washington, while describing Tehran’s political decision-making system as “very confused”. In an interview with journalist Vince Coglianese, Vance said President Donald Trump had made clear that “there is a universe where we can strike a deal with Iran, but that requires the Iranians to behave”. He said Washington’s approach would be based on Iranian actions rather than statements. Vance said Iran’s leadership involved “a number of different constituencies”, including hardliners, conservatives, moderates and clerics. He also said Iran’s new supreme leader was “very detached” and not involved in day-to-day decision-making or public discussions about negotiations.

An Iran war in which Trump promised quick victory has turned into a protracted farce dragging down the world economy. The president’s “reciprocal tariffs” were gutted by the Supreme Court, and his administration’s trade agenda remains deeply unpopular . items.title: Ex-Biden officials are desperate for a Gaza scapegoat
items.summary: There’s something profoundly human about the scapegoat. From the ancient Israelites and Greeks to the Aztecs , global cultures have long sought to concentrate society’s ills in a single vessel, cleansing the rest of us in the process. Today, the Democratic foreign-policy establishment is looking for a scapegoat of its own. Tainted by the sins of enabling Israeli conduct in Gaza and beyond, many national-security mandarins are seeking absolution by proxy, perhaps in hopes of returning to the halls of power in 2029. Joe Biden has emerged as the bearer of these iniquities. items.title: Iran supreme leader says US will be forced out of Middle East
items.summary: Iran supreme leader says US will be forced out of Middle East Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei said on Monday that the United States would be forced to leave the Middle East after suffering "painful blows", according to a statement carried by state television. Khamenei, who has not been seen in public since the start of the war in late February, made the remarks despite attempts to revive talks aimed at ending the fighting. "Today, having suffered painful blows at the hands of valiant fighters and the guardians of the Strait of Hormuz, they (the enemies) do not venture beyond the Arabian Sea," Khamenei said in the written statement attributed to him, without explicitly mentioning the United States. "Whenever they have braved this risk, they have only brought harm upon themselves. It will not be long before the Arabian Sea, too, would rid itself of their presence," he added.

clusters.headline: Palestinian-American journalist freed after 13 days in Israeli detention

items.title: Palestinian-American journalist freed after 13 days in Israeli detention
items.summary: Palestinian-American journalist freed after 13 days in Israeli detention Palestinian-American journalist Naqaa Hamed was released from Damon Prison after 13 days, following an Israeli court decision. Hamed was arrested on 15 September at the Tuqu checkpoint while returning from an assignment, was separated from her camera crew and taken to an unknown location for questioning. Hamed was arrested on suspicion of “cooperating with an enemy entity” and possible espionage, according to Israeli media at the time. She previously served as a correspondent for Iran’s Press TV in the occupied West Bank. According to the Palestinian Prisoners’ Society, 36 Palestinian journalists, including four women, remain detained in Israeli jails, along with about 90 Palestinian women.

clusters.headline: Why does the US control Iraq's oil revenues?

items.title: Why does the US control Iraq's oil revenues?
items.summary: Why does the US control Iraq's oil revenues? For more than two decades, Iraq 's oil wealth has passed through a financial system centred thousands of miles away in New York. The arrangement, created after the US -led invasion of Iraq in 2003, was initially designed to protect Iraqi oil revenues from creditors and help fund reconstruction. Today, it gives Washington significant leverage over Iraq's access to its own dollars, leverage that the US is increasingly using as it pressures Baghdad to curb Iran 's influence and the activities of armed groups aligned with Tehran. The issue came into sharp focus in April, when Washington blocked a shipment of about $500m in cash to Iraq as it pressured the government over Iran-aligned armed groups. Muayen al-Kadhimi, a former parliamentary Finance Committee member, condemned the decision at the time, calling on the government to end what he described as US dominance over Iraqi funds. Read more: Why does the US control Iraq's oil revenues?

items.summary: Renewed fighting between Iran-aligned Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni forces has shattered four years of relative calm In the mornings, 13-year-old Muneer Farie went to school, and in the afternoons he helped his father feed the livestock. He took his studies seriously, dreaming of becoming the first teacher in his family of farmers. As fighting approached his village in al-Wazeyah district in Taiz, Yemen, two weeks ago, Muneer’s focus started to drift from his lessons. The classroom echoed with the distant sounds of explosions and gunfire. His home was suddenly on the frontline of renewed fighting between the Iran-aligned Houthis and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government. Continue reading...

items.title: Israel wants US-led force to disarm Lebanon's Hezbollah
items.summary: Fearing a security vacuum if UN peacekeepers leave southern Lebanon when their mandate expires December 31, the Lebanese government is desperately seeking an extension of the United Nations Interim Force (UNIFIL) or the creation of a European-led multinational force to take its place. Israel, which has occupied dozens of villages south of the Litani River since its latest invasion of the country earlier this year can't wait for the Blue Helmets to leave. It has long lobbied against UNIFIL’s extension, deeming it ineffective in taming and disarming Hezbollah, the Iran-backed militia. But Tel Aviv hasn't opposed an international force once UNIFIL leaves; it just doesn’t want one tied to the UN. Israel is lobbying for a U.S.-led force, while the Lebanese government prefers a European-led mission to aid the Lebanese army if UNIFIL’s mandate is not renewed or extended. An even bigger question is how exactly any such force can subdue battle-hardened Hezbollah, the country’s most powerful armed force. De arrestaties waren in de buurt van de luchtmachtbasis van de Royal Air Force bij Fairford in het graafschap Gloucestershire. Daar zijn behalve Britse militairen ook Amerikaanse militairen en bommenwerpers gestationeerd die actief zijn in de oorlog tegen Iran. De arrestaties volgden op een telefoontje van een inwoner naar de politie aan het begin van de nacht over drie verdachte voertuigen die op weg waren naar de basis, RAF Fairford. Een gebied in een straal van 400 meter rond de voertuigen is sinds vannacht afgezet. De drie witte busjes worden onderzocht door de explosievenopruimingsdienst. Op beelden is te zien dat een robot heen en weer rijdt tussen de voertuigen. Bij de busjes liggen grote zwarte voorwerpen verspreid op de grond. items.summary: ¿Quién manda en Irán? Hasta que Donald Trump y Benjamin Netanyahu decidieron lanzar su guerra sorpresa contra Teherán el 28 de febrero , la respuesta era clara: el líder supremo, Alí Jamenei. Ese mismo día, Estados Unidos e Israel asesinaron a Jamenei, máxima autoridad desde que tomó el relevo de Ruhola Jomeini en 1989.Las autoridades islámicas tardaron un mes en llenar ese vacío de poder y designaron a Mojtaba , su hijo, como nuevo guía del país. Ha pasado un intenso medio año desde su nombramiento oficial y su paradero es toda una incógnita. Ni vídeos, ni fotografías, ni mensajes de voz.La única comunicación del líder de la república islámica con el exterior ha sido a través de una serie de textos que le han atribuido y compartido los medios oficiales . Nada más. De basis wordt sinds maart door de Amerikanen gebruikt voor bombardementsvluchten op Iran. Prince Faisal, who led the Saudi delegation at the meeting, added that Riyadh supports efforts to reduce tensions in the region and stressed that "any arrangements for its security be comprehensive". He also supported initiatives aimed at de-escalation, particularly efforts by Qatar and Pakistan, saying they can help restore regional stability. The minister accused Iran of flagrant attacks on civilian and economic targets across the region, while calling on the international community to condemn Houthi actions threatening Red Sea shipping.

"At my direction, teams were dispatched across the globe to engage with countries and demand action against the Iranian regime," he said on X. “These efforts are delivering results,” he wrote. Bessent noted that Turkey and Oman have halted incoming flights from private carrier Mahan Air, while the United Arab Emirates has stopped all flights by Iranian airlines. Dubai, the UAE's commercial hub, is a major destination for Iran's carriers, with multiple daily flights, a large Iranian community and close business links. Talaei-Nik said the United States had failed to achieve its strategic objectives in the war on Iran, including efforts to weaken Iran’s strategic position in the region. He said Iran had instead “imposed costs on the enemy”, according to Tasnim. The defence ministry spokesman also said Iran needed to simultaneously strengthen its defence capabilities and domestic capacity. His comments come as Tehran continues to assess the impact of the war and reinforce its military infrastructure.

items.summary: Pezeshkian says Iran will allow UN nuclear inspectors to return Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has said that his country would allow UN nuclear inspectors into the country, CBS News reported. In an interview with CBS News, Pezeshkian said: “If they wish to come in and have inspections, we can reach accords and agreements vis-a-vis that specific topic within the negotiations.” At the same time, Pezeshkian reiterated that Iran is not trying to build a nuclear weapon. items.summary: EU warns of energy 'price crisis', asks countries to consider curbing demand The European Union is facing an energy price crisis as a result of the Iran war fallout in oil and gas markets, the bloc's energy chief said on Friday in a letter seen by Reuters, which urged countries to consider measures to curb energy demand. "We are facing a price crisis linking to a supply crisis," EU energy commissioner Dan Jorgensen said in a letter to EU countries' energy ministers. While the EU is better prepared now than it was in winter 2021 when Russia squeezed Europe's gas supplies by reducing deliveries, governments must step up preparations for this winter, he said. "I invite you to consider taking or continuing to take measures that can sustain [gas storage] injections or reduce gas and electricity demand for as long as necessary," Jorgensen said.

Hours earlier, Iraq’s state news agency had also reported the suspension of Iranian flights at Najaf International Airport over threats of US sanctions. The move means flights to and from Iran have been suspended at all four Iraqi airports where Iranian airlines were operating – Baghdad, Najaf, Erbil and Sulaimaniya – two sources told Reuters. These systems provide multiple layers of protection for the building but they also carry a risk of backfiring: any surveillance system that is vulnerable to intruders could potentially provide unauthorized users with details about the activities of the Defense Department (DOD) and its employees. This risk is higher than usual right now because of the decision to install a controversial piece of equipment all over the Pentagon grounds: Flock cameras. There are at least nine Flock automated license plate readers (ALPRs) currently monitoring the traffic lanes used by drivers entering the Pentagon’s parking lots, including many of the DOD’s own employees. items.title: Why South Korea won’t send military to Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Since the U.S. war against Iran started earlier this year, Washington has pressed its allies in Europe and Asia to “ step up ” with military aid to help the United States reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Despite persistent pressure from both Trump administration officials and President Donald Trump himself , most U.S. allies have remained reluctant . Those who have chosen to provide support have done so largely in an indirect capacity, such as by permitting limited base access. South Korea has been a major target of that pressure. In August, Trump abruptly announced on social media that Washington will “substantially reduce” U.S.-South Korea joint military exercises, linking the decision to Seoul’s continued refusal to support his war efforts against Iran. Trump’s apparent retaliation alarmed Seoul and sparked a serious debate over whether to deploy its navy to the Strait of Hormuz. items.title: The US kill count in Iran makes the phrase ‘precision strikes’ absurd
items.summary: When the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran ultimately ends, it will be remembered for its bloody onset. On the same day airstrikes killed the Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in Tehran, a U.S. missile incinerated an elementary school in Minab, killing 123 children and dozens of others. Some 250 miles away, U.S. missiles fell on a residential area of Lamerd, killing 21 civilians, including five children. Neither the White House nor Pentagon has publicly admitted responsibility in either incident, although an internal review reportedly determined Minab was hit by a U.S. missile. items.title: Iran says Hormuz Strait to remain closed until US meets seven conditions
items.summary: Iran says Hormuz Strait to remain closed until US meets seven conditions Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has said that the Strait of Hormuz will remain shut until Washington meets certain conditions. Ghalibaf, who also acts as Tehran's chief negotiator in the talks, said that the contested waterway will remain closed until seven conditions based on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding are met by Washington. He conceded that the US had made "some proposals through a mediator" after Tehran presented a seven-day roadmap to reopen the strait. But he warned Washington that "the era of wasting time and dictating unilateral demands is over" and Iran's position remains "clear and definite".

items.title: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman: Strait of Hormuz 'main concern' of leadership
items.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman: Strait of Hormuz 'main concern' of leadership Iran's foreign ministry spokesman, Esmaeil Baghaei, has said that the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz is the "main focus" of truce talks with Washington. Speaking at a news conference, Baghaei said that Tehran is "focusing on the strait foremost", and that its primary concern is "to reach a solution and to have peace and stability restored within this waterway".  He added that, by contrast, Washington's strategy to end the conflict is focused on Iran's nuclear file. He told reporters that the return of International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) inspectors has not been discussed by Iran's leadership. He noted that the peace process has been thwarted by the "volatility and fluctuation" of Washington's decision-making. “This is reflected in their conflicting statements as well as their fluctuating demands. items.title: Three commercial vessels struck in Hormuz since 1 Oct, UKMTO says
items.summary: Three commercial vessels struck in Hormuz since 1 Oct, UKMTO says Attacks on commercial ships witnessed a surge during the past three days, as at least three tankers were struck by unidentified projectiles in and around the Strait of Hormuz, according to United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) warnings. Early Saturday, UKMTO reported that a crude oil tanker was hit on its port side approximately 4 nautical miles east of Oman. A day earlier, an outbound vessel suffered a small fire and blackout, while a second crude tanker was struck nearby. On Thursday, a supertanker carrying 2.5 million barrels caught fire after being hit off Oman while transiting an unauthorised route, according to Iran's Fars news agency. In its weekly Voluntary Reporting Area Overview released on 2 October, UKMTO said 91 incidents of damage to vessels have been reported since February this year. Three tankers have been struck in and around the Strait of Hormuz since 1 October 2026. (AFP)

items.title: Iran's warns 'half-a-century-old' UAE over claim on three Gulf islands
items.summary: Iran's warns 'half-a-century-old' UAE over claim on three Gulf islands Ali Akbar Velayati, a senior adviser to Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, has warned the United Arab Emirates (UAE) against challenging Tehran and its sovereignty over three islands in the Persian Gulf. In a post on his X account, Velayati dismissed recent claims made by the UAE at the United Nations General Assembly regarding sovereignty over Greater Tunb, Lesser Tunb, and Abu Musa, saying the three islands will remain Iranian forever, according to IRNA. "A country whose political life does not reach half a century makes claims from the UN podium about islands that have been recorded under Iran's name in historical documents and maps of past centuries," Velayati said in the Farsi-language post. He added that the UAE should not "rely on foreign powers" for its security and should instead pursue good relations with its neighbours, IRNA reported. "The neighbour stays, and the guest goes… Regional experience has shown that imported security has an expiration date," said the former Iranian foreign minister.

items.title: State Department says Iranian UN delegation duo expelled from US
items.summary: State Department says Iranian UN delegation duo expelled from US The United States has expelled two members of the Iranian delegation who attended the recent UN General Assembly after they ignored an order to leave the country, the State Department said Saturday. "Two more members of the Iranian delegation were found still in (New York) long after the United Nations General Assembly had passed. They have now been kicked out of the US," a US official told AFP, adding that Secretary of State Marco Rubio "means business." US media reported the State Department had told Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his delegation to leave the country Monday, and resorted to expelling the two members after learning from the Iranian mission to the UN they remained in the country on Friday. One member of the delegation left Friday night, while the second departed Saturday morning, according to Axios.

items.summary: Iranian rial at new low, as cenbank sells dollars to support currency Iran's rial continued its decline on Saturday, as the central bank announced an injection of up to $2 billion to support the currency while the economy faces US sanctions and a naval blockade. The US dollar was sold at around 2.688 million rials, up from 2.632 million on Friday, according to free-market tracking website bon-bast.com, while alanchand.com reported 2.695 million rials per dollar. State television said state banks began selling up to $2 billion to support the currency, which has lost more than half of its value in the past year. With an inflation rate of more than 70 percent, life is becoming ever tougher for ordinary citizens unable to afford basic necessities or rent ​as a US blockade cuts the state's financial lifeline – oil exports. Many Iranians seeking safe havens for their savings have been buying dollars, other hard currencies or gold.

Trump era andato giù duro, dicendo che la premier gli aveva «fatto pena». Meloni aveva reagito definendo quelle dichiarazioni «totalmente inventate» e dicendosi «allibita». Già nel mese di luglio il presidente statunitense aveva abbassato i toni, definendo Meloni una «brava persona» ma aveva criticato la posizione dell'italia sul conflitto con l’Iran. items.title: L'Inde et sa stratégie de corridors
items.summary: En Inde, dès que l'on parle de sanctions contre la Russie ou bien l'Iran, c'est le transport qui en paye le prix. Fin septembre, le président américain Donald Trump a renforcé sa loi sur les tarifs douaniers contre la Russie. Ces sanctions s'adressent aussi à tous les pays qui commercent avec Moscou. Or, l'Inde, pénalisée par la guerre au Moyen-Orient et la fermeture du détroit d'Ormuz, a continué d'importer du pétrole russe. Dans ses derniers articles pour l'Institut de relations internationales et stratégiques (Iris), Olivier Da Lage, ancien journaliste à RFI et spécialiste de l'Inde, explique comment le pays cherche à bâtir de nouvelles routes pour diversifier son commerce.

items.title: Iraq given US exemption for Iranian flights to and from holy city
items.summary: Iraq given US exemption for Iranian flights to and from holy city The United States has granted sanctions exemptions for some Iranian airlines to operate flights to Iraq's holy city of Najaf, the Iraqi prime minister's office said on Friday. It said Baghdad had secured "an agreement allowing Iranian airlines, with the exception of Mahan Air, to operate 40 flights daily to and from Najaf" , a city sacred to Shia Muslims. The US announced sweeping new sanctions targeting Iranian airlines last month as part of its efforts to pressure Iran's economy, with the two sides still to make peace in Washington's war on Tehran. Last week, Najaf airport suspended all Iranian flights in cooperation with the sanctions, leaving travellers scrambling for alternative routes.

The Houthis, officially called Ansar Allah, have seized territory in Yemen's southwest this month in a rapid offensive triggered by the Saudi bombing of Sanaa airport in July. Seen up close, it is a study in stasis and decline UN general assembly meetings are not usually riveting occasions. But this year’s encapsulated a world in flux and crisis, an international law and organisation structure that is falling apart, and a humanitarian order machine running hot. What unfolded was less a gathering for resolution and resolve than a display of showboating, frustration and fractiousness. It was a snapshot for the history books of four huge destabilising conflicts for which there seems to be no means of, or interest in, resolution – Ukraine, Iran, Palestine and Sudan. items.title: Gen. Burhan digs in as Trump's visa-for-ceasefire scheme blows up
items.summary: On the morning of September 24, Abdel Fattah Burhan should have been standing at the podium of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. Instead, he was in Khartoum. The general who leads Sudan’s army and chairs its Sovereignty Council had been offered his American visa on a condition, which, as detailed by Reuters, involved signing the 90-day ceasefire that Massad Boulos, President Donald Trump’s adviser for Arab and African affairs, had been pitching for months. Burhan rejected the condition, telling a crowded stadium in Khartoum on September 26 that “we do not want a visa to any country...we will stay here with you until we die here in this country.” This episode caps a year in which American policy toward Sudan’s civil war has steadily become more hostile toward Burhan and his Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) — the very party that Boulos in a May interview called the “constitutional institution” that must be preserved. items.title: Goodnight Baghdad: US troops leave Iraq after 23 years
items.summary: The Iraq War was already four-years-old when I walked down the ramp of a C-17 at Al Taqaddum Air Base in April 2007. The fact that I am writing these words is proof that I survived that deployment and a subsequent one to Afghanistan in 2013. In the years since, I transitioned back into civilian life, established a new career, and saw my kids grow up and escape the nest. During nearly all of that time, there were still American troops on the ground in Iraq. I have a son serving in the military today. He has never been to Iraq, but I can absolutely sympathize with the Iraq veterans who came home from the war only to see their sons or daughters deploy to the same war zone. items.title: Venezuela blowback may have a long fuse. It always does.
items.summary: In 1927, Augusto Cesar Sandino began an insurgent campaign against the U.S. occupation of Nicaragua. Under orders from President Calvin Coolidge, the U.S. Marines had intervened in Nicaragua to settle a civil war between a conservative government and liberal rebels. In his manifesto , Sandino responded by effectively declaring war on the United States. He also specifically denounced former liberal leaders who had agreed to put down their arms in the face of U.S. intervention. Speaking of General Moncada, the leading liberal officer who had agreed to end his revolt in talks convened by future Secretary of State Henry Stimson, Sandino wrote: “Nobody gave him the authority to abandon the ranks of the revolution to make secret agreements with the enemy.” One imagines there are Chavistas in Venezuela with similar feelings about interim President Delcy Rodriguez right now. Having intervened to end the civil war in Nicaragua, the U.S. soon found itself embroiled in a bitter counter-insurgency campaign against Sandino’s men. items.title: Vance describes Iran’s leadership as ‘very confused’, says deal possible
items.summary: Vance describes Iran’s leadership as ‘very confused’, says deal possible US Vice President JD Vance said there is still scope for a deal with Iran if its leaders honour their commitments to Washington, while describing Tehran’s political decision-making system as “very confused”. In an interview with journalist Vince Coglianese, Vance said President Donald Trump had made clear that “there is a universe where we can strike a deal with Iran, but that requires the Iranians to behave”. He said Washington’s approach would be based on Iranian actions rather than statements. Vance said Iran’s leadership involved “a number of different constituencies”, including hardliners, conservatives, moderates and clerics. He also said Iran’s new supreme leader was “very detached” and not involved in day-to-day decision-making or public discussions about negotiations.

items.title: Lessons from the Iran War
items.summary: The Iran war offers broader lessons about the limits of force, the resilience of revolutionary regimes, and the unpredictability of modern conflict. Military action can weaken an adversary without producing decisive political outcomes, while economic pressure, alliances, energy markets, and public opinion can prove equally consequential. The conflict also exposed vulnerabilities in alliance coordination, munitions stocks, counter-drone capabilities, and strategic communication. Effective deterrence ultimately requires hard power, resilient partnerships, clear objectives, and the political will to sustain them.

First, the inflationary risks of throwing subsidies at the housing market at a moment when wider inflation, driven by energy prices and the Iran war, is on the march. Second, the political awkwardness of turning to George Osborne’s playbook. Third, the spectre of Jeff Fairburn, the shameless former boss of Persimmon who bagged a £75m bonus in 2018 as help to buy turbo-charged the value of his share-based incentives. items.summary: Iran supreme leader says US will be forced out of Middle East Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei said on Monday that the United States would be forced to leave the Middle East after suffering "painful blows", according to a statement carried by state television. Khamenei, who has not been seen in public since the start of the war in late February, made the remarks despite attempts to revive talks aimed at ending the fighting. "Today, having suffered painful blows at the hands of valiant fighters and the guardians of the Strait of Hormuz, they (the enemies) do not venture beyond the Arabian Sea," Khamenei said in the written statement attributed to him, without explicitly mentioning the United States. "Whenever they have braved this risk, they have only brought harm upon themselves. It will not be long before the Arabian Sea, too, would rid itself of their presence," he added.

items.title: Why does the US control Iraq's oil revenues?
items.summary: Why does the US control Iraq's oil revenues? For more than two decades, Iraq 's oil wealth has passed through a financial system centred thousands of miles away in New York. The arrangement, created after the US -led invasion of Iraq in 2003, was initially designed to protect Iraqi oil revenues from creditors and help fund reconstruction. Today, it gives Washington significant leverage over Iraq's access to its own dollars, leverage that the US is increasingly using as it pressures Baghdad to curb Iran 's influence and the activities of armed groups aligned with Tehran. The issue came into sharp focus in April, when Washington blocked a shipment of about $500m in cash to Iraq as it pressured the government over Iran-aligned armed groups. Muayen al-Kadhimi, a former parliamentary Finance Committee member, condemned the decision at the time, calling on the government to end what he described as US dominance over Iraqi funds. Read more: Why does the US control Iraq's oil revenues?

items.title: Israel wants US-led force to disarm Lebanon's Hezbollah
items.summary: Fearing a security vacuum if UN peacekeepers leave southern Lebanon when their mandate expires December 31, the Lebanese government is desperately seeking an extension of the United Nations Interim Force (UNIFIL) or the creation of a European-led multinational force to take its place. Israel, which has occupied dozens of villages south of the Litani River since its latest invasion of the country earlier this year can't wait for the Blue Helmets to leave. It has long lobbied against UNIFIL’s extension, deeming it ineffective in taming and disarming Hezbollah, the Iran-backed militia. But Tel Aviv hasn't opposed an international force once UNIFIL leaves; it just doesn’t want one tied to the UN. Israel is lobbying for a U.S.-led force, while the Lebanese government prefers a European-led mission to aid the Lebanese army if UNIFIL’s mandate is not renewed or extended. An even bigger question is how exactly any such force can subdue battle-hardened Hezbollah, the country’s most powerful armed force. De arrestaties waren in de buurt van de luchtmachtbasis van de Royal Air Force bij Fairford in het graafschap Gloucestershire. Daar zijn behalve Britse militairen ook Amerikaanse militairen en bommenwerpers gestationeerd die actief zijn in de oorlog tegen Iran. De arrestaties volgden op een telefoontje van een inwoner naar de politie aan het begin van de nacht over drie verdachte voertuigen die op weg waren naar de basis, RAF Fairford. items.title: Irán, siete meses bajo un líder invisible
items.summary: ¿Quién manda en Irán? Hasta que Donald Trump y Benjamin Netanyahu decidieron lanzar su guerra sorpresa contra Teherán el 28 de febrero , la respuesta era clara: el líder supremo, Alí Jamenei. Ese mismo día, Estados Unidos e Israel asesinaron a Jamenei, máxima autoridad desde que tomó el relevo de Ruhola Jomeini en 1989.Las autoridades islámicas tardaron un mes en llenar ese vacío de poder y designaron a Mojtaba , su hijo, como nuevo guía del país. Ha pasado un intenso medio año desde su nombramiento oficial y su paradero es toda una incógnita. Ni vídeos, ni fotografías, ni mensajes de voz.La única comunicación del líder de la república islámica con el exterior ha sido a través de una serie de textos que le han atribuido y compartido los medios oficiales . Nada más. items.summary: Gaat de VS het hele Internationaal Strafhof op de sanctielijst zetten? In Den Haag maar ook in Brussel zijn alle ogen gericht op Washington, dat dreigt het Hof "steen voor steen" af te breken. "Handen af van het Internationaal Strafhof", zei premier Jetten eerder deze week in New York bij de Verenigde Naties. Nederland krijgt steun van Europese bondgenoten. "Bedreigingen en aanvallen tegen het Internationaal Strafhof zijn onaanvaardbaar", zei de voorzitter van de Europese Raad Antonio Costa. In zijn toespraak een dag eerder sprak de Amerikaanse president Trump over "schijnprocessen" van het Hof. Maar hij kondigde nog geen verdergaande sancties aan - volgens Jetten een gevolg van de stille diplomatie waar Nederland al tijden mee bezig is. Jetten reageerde bij de Verenigde Naties op de aanval op het Strafhof: Hoelang die strategie blijft werken, is onzeker. Nederland heeft als gastland een speciale verantwoordelijkheid, zegt de regering. Dat betekent ook dat Den Haag extra kwetsbaar is voor Trumps toorn in zijn hetze tegen het hof. items.summary: Bij een Britse luchtmachtbasis in het graafschap Gloucestershire is vanmorgen groot alarm geslagen in verband met een veiligheidsincident. De explosievenopruimingsdienst onderzoekt of er in auto's in de buurt van de basis explosieven zitten. Er wordt onder meer een robot ingezet om drie witte bestelbusjes te doorzoeken. Uit beelden blijkt dat uit zeker een busje zwarte vaten zijn gehaald: Het onderzoek wordt geleid door de contraterrorisme-afdeling van de Britse politie. Voorafgaand aan de operatie is een aantal mannen opgepakt. Hoeveel er dat zijn en wat hun identiteit is, heeft de politie niet bekendgemaakt. Op de RAF-basis Fairford zijn behalve Britse militairen ook een groot aantal Amerikaanse militairen gelegerd. De basis wordt sinds maart door de Amerikanen gebruikt voor bombardementsvluchten op Iran. Iranian airlines mainly carry Iraqi Shia pilgrims to Iran's holy cities or Iranians visiting sacred sites in Iraq. items.summary: Riyadh schools to operate remotely for week, AFP reports Parents across Riyadh received emails from schools on Sunday announcing a last-minute plan to shift to remote learning for a week, according to messages seen by AFP. "We have just been informed by Saudi authorities that schools must remain closed all week," read two separate messages seen by AFP. There was no official reason given but the move comes amid heightened tensions in the Gulf and near-daily attacks aimed at Saudi Arabia by Iran-backed Houthi fighters in Yemen. "When a decision affects an entire school community for a full week, families deserve clear communication and transparency about the reasons behind it," one parent living in Riyadh who spoke on condition of anonymity told AFP. "It's a last-minute decision. We have no clue what's happening," a Lebanese expatriate living in Riyadh added. items.title: US ships in Indian Ocean will be hit if US launches new attacks, IRGC says
items.summary: US ships in Indian Ocean will be hit if US launches new attacks, IRGC says Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has warned it will attack US warships, even those in the Indian Ocean, if Washington launches new attacks against Iran, Iranian media reported. “If Trump considers the Strait of Hormuz his strait, then why aren’t his ships and vessels here?” Ali Mohammadi, the IRGC Navy’s deputy for political affairs, said, according to the Fars news agency. On Saturday, Trump posted an image on his Truth Social platform showing the Strait of Hormuz circled and labelled “Trump Strait”, hours after Iran said it had presented a seven-day plan to reopen the strategic waterway. Mohammadi said the US “should just bring one of its ships close to this area” if it claims to control the waterway. “If another war breaks out, we will undoubtedly attack and hit their ships and destroyers even in the Indian Ocean,” he warned.

items.summary: Saudi Arabia calls for 'comprehensive' regional navigation security Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan used his address at the UN General Assembly to call for serious international cooperation to protect freedom of navigation and stress that regional security framework should be "comprehensive". “Protecting international navigation is a shared responsibility that requires serious international cooperation,” he said. Prince Faisal, who led the Saudi delegation at the meeting, added that Riyadh supports efforts to reduce tensions in the region and stressed that "any arrangements for its security be comprehensive". He also supported initiatives aimed at de-escalation, particularly efforts by Qatar and Pakistan, saying they can help restore regional stability. The minister accused Iran of flagrant attacks on civilian and economic targets across the region, while calling on the international community to condemn Houthi actions threatening Red Sea shipping.

items.summary: US thanks Turkey, Oman, UAE for supporting sanctions against Iran US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has thanked the governments of the United Kingdom, Turkey, Oman and the UAE for supporting Washington’s "Operation Economic Outcast", a harsh economic campaign against Iran. "At my direction, teams were dispatched across the globe to engage with countries and demand action against the Iranian regime," he said on X. “These efforts are delivering results,” he wrote. Bessent noted that Turkey and Oman have halted incoming flights from private carrier Mahan Air, while the United Arab Emirates has stopped all flights by Iranian airlines. Dubai, the UAE's commercial hub, is a major destination for Iran's carriers, with multiple daily flights, a large Iranian community and close business links. Bessent also highlighted new banking restrictions. On Wednesday, the UAE central bank blocked transactions to and from Iran by branches of Iran's Bank Melli, accusing it of violating laws on money laundering, terrorism and arms proliferation. items.title: Pezeshkian says Iran no longer trusts negotiations with US
items.summary: Pezeshkian says Iran no longer trusts negotiations with US Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has told Al Jazeera that Iran no longer trusts negotiations with the United States after previous rounds of talks were followed by attacks and sanctions. "The day after the US president's speech, it was our turn to speak. In effect, he threatened to wipe Iran off the map and labelled us as 'terrorist'," he said. "This is the fourth or fifth time we have held talks. What has happened, and continues to happen is that we no longer trust these talks. No matter how much we negotiate, after a while they start attacking us, imposing sanctions and taking the kinds of actions they have taken before." "At least we have reached an understanding on a framework and announced it. Now the Americans have to respond. Are they willing to move within this framework, or do they want to derail the process again?" the president said. Pezeshkian told Al Jazeera that previous rounds of talks were followed by attacks and sanctions. (AFP)

items.title: At UN, Saudi FM warns world failing to protect Gulf shipping
items.summary: At UN, Saudi FM warns world failing to protect Gulf shipping Saudi Arabia warned UN members Saturday that attempts to block Middle East waterways are a threat to global energy security and demanded the international community do more to defend freedom of navigation. Since the United States and Israel launched their war on Iran in late February, Tehran has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, while its Houthi allies in Yemen have subsequently done the same in the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Both waterways are vital routes for oil and gas exports. "The international community has been absent from assuming its responsibilities in confronting all that threatens international peace and security," Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan told the United Nations General Assembly. "The kingdom stresses the importance of guaranteeing the protection of freedom of navigation in all international waterways, foremost among them the Strait of Hormuz, the Bab al-Mandab Strait, the Red Sea, the Gulf of Aden," he said.

items.summary: Trump rejects Iranian proposal to open Hormuz and end war US President Donald Trump said on Saturday he had rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the Iran war. Iran raised the initiative at the UN General Assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted to the Americans via Qatari mediators and that it could reopen the strategic waterway and put an end to hostilities in the region within seven days. But in comments to reporters at the White House, Trump said: "I reject their proposal. ... I rejected their deal. "They want to make a deal to open the Hormuz Strait immediately because they're losing so badly," he said before leaving for Tennessee. "We're winning tremendously. "They want to make a deal and I think that's fine, I like making a deal too. What they want to do is immediately open the Hormuz Strait ... because they have no money coming in, because they get their money from the Hormuz Strait," Trump said.

Talaei-Nik said the United States had failed to achieve its strategic objectives in the war on Iran, including efforts to weaken Iran’s strategic position in the region. His comments come as Tehran continues to assess the impact of the war and reinforce its military infrastructure.

items.title: Report: Trump rejects Iran's ceasefire proposal, may resume bombing after midterms
items.summary: Report: Trump rejects Iran's ceasefire proposal, may resume bombing after midterms President Trump has rejected Iran’s proposal for a seven-day ceasefire and has told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November midterms, The Wall Street Journal reported. Citing officials, the newspaper reported that Trump is reluctant to resume major combat operations, while noting his views could change and that he could also end up being swayed by the midterm results. Tehran’s proposal would have reopened the Strait of Hormuz and resumed nuclear talks in return for the US lifting its blockade of Iranian ports, which is causing serious damage to the country’s economy.

items.title: Iran proposes plan to reopen Hormuz within seven days
items.summary: Iran proposes plan to reopen Hormuz within seven days Araghchi met for talks on Tuesday with US President Donald Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff, and previously set out conditions for ending the war and reopening the vital energy shipping channel. "Iran has conveyed to the United States, through Qatar, a concrete seven-day plan. If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, and normal maritime passage restored within seven days," Araghchi said at the UN Friday. "The choice now rests with the United States. Iran does not accept coercion, threats, or intimidation, and Iran will not surrender its sovereign rights under pressure. "I can tell you if there is seriousness in the US side to come to a deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, everything is now prepared." Earlier media reports suggest the new plan calls for a seven-day cessation of all hostilities in the Middle East, including in Lebanon.

items.title: EU warns of energy 'price crisis', asks countries to consider curbing demand
items.summary: EU warns of energy 'price crisis', asks countries to consider curbing demand The European Union is facing an energy price crisis as a result of the Iran war fallout in oil and gas markets, the bloc's energy chief said on Friday in a letter seen by Reuters, which urged countries to consider measures to curb energy demand. "We are facing a price crisis linking to a supply crisis," EU energy commissioner Dan Jorgensen said in a letter to EU countries' energy ministers. While the EU is better prepared now than it was in winter 2021 when Russia squeezed Europe's gas supplies by reducing deliveries, governments must step up preparations for this winter, he said. "I invite you to consider taking or continuing to take measures that can sustain [gas storage] injections or reduce gas and electricity demand for as long as necessary," Jorgensen said.

items.summary: Colombia's new US-backed government cuts ties with Iran Colombia said on Thursday it had cut diplomatic ties with Iran, the latest Washington ally in Latin America to sever links with the US arch-foe. Colombia's new right-wing president, Abelardo de la Espriella, has redrawn Colombia's alliances since taking over from his leftist predecessor Gustavo Petro on 7 August with the full-throated endorsement of US President Donald Trump. De la Espriella's government accused the Iranian government of having ties to "narco-terrorist groups that threaten the security of the country," without giving proof of the allegations. Iran's foreign ministry hit back on Friday, calling the allegations "baseless claims". "It is clear that none of the claims put forward by the Colombian government to justify this decision are valid or logical, and that this decision has been made solely under the influence of the Zionist regime and the United States."

In the five days left before the proposed reopening of the strait, which is expected to relieve pressure on global energy markets, Trump would need to lift Iranian asset freezes, permit Iran to export its oil and, probably most difficult of all, order Benjamin Netanyahu to end Israel’s attacks on Hezbollah in Lebanon, thus achieving the “ceasefire on all fronts”.
